text:
BlinkIt has increasingly started to feel like a company that operates entirely at its own convenience, with very little consideration for its customers. Orders can apparently be cancelled even after taking an advance payment, without properly informing the customer or seeking their consent.

If a company accepts an advance payment and confirms an order, it should not be able to simply cancel it whenever it suits them, leaving the customer to deal with the inconvenience. At the very least, customers deserve proper communication, transparency, and a choice before such a decision is made.

This kind of one-sided approach is rude, inappropriate, and deeply disappointing. A customer-centric company should respect the customer’s time, money, and consent—not treat orders as something it can change or cancel at its own convenience.

Despite clearly explaining that three products were missing, I did not receive the support or resolution I expected. As a loyal customer, I expected my concern to be taken seriously, but I was left feeling ignored and frustrated.

I use Blinkit almost every day and have always preferred it over other grocery delivery apps because of its convenience and reliability. Unfortunately, this incident has completely shaken my trust in the platform. Missing multiple products in a single order reflects a serious failure in quality control, and poor customer support only makes the situation worse.

Customers should not have to waste their time proving that products were missing, repeatedly contacting support, or struggling to get a fair resolution for mistakes that were not theirs. This entire experience has been stressful, frustrating, and highly disappointing.

I sincerely hope Blinkit improves both its order verification process and its customer support. Until then, I cannot confidently recommend Blinkit, especially for expensive or high-value orders. title: Food safety concerns
text:
My experience with Blinkit has been extremely disappointing and concerning.

I ordered ice cream, and although it arrived frozen, it was obvious that it had melted previously and had been re-frozen before delivery. The texture and condition clearly indicated this. I immediately provided Blinkit with photos and videos as evidence.

This is not just a quality issue—it raises serious food safety concerns. Ice cream is a dairy product, and if it melts and is then re-frozen, it can become unsafe to consume and may no longer meet acceptable food safety standards. Selling products in this condition is unacceptable and could put customers’ health at risk.

Instead of issuing a proper refund, Blinkit told me they had provided a ₹200 refund as a coupon code. However, when I placed my next order, there was no option anywhere in the app to enter or redeem the coupon code. A refund that cannot actually be used is not a refund.

To make matters worse, I spent a long time dealing with Blinkit’s chatbot, with no meaningful resolution and no easy way to contact a real customer support representative.

Between the questionable condition of the food, the unusable refund coupon, and the lack of accessible customer support, this has been one of the worst customer service experiences I’ve had. Blinkit needs to take food quality and customer safety far more seriously. I cannot recommend this service.

title: Important: Verify the Weight of Meat Ordered Online
text:
Just a heads-up for everyone ordering chicken from Blinkit.

Today I ordered a 450 g pack of Godrej boneless chicken. I usually don’t check the weight, but this time I was making a recipe that required exactly 450 g, so I placed it on my kitchen weighing scale.

To my surprise, the pack weighed only 380 g, not 450 g.

I contacted Blinkit, and they promptly refunded me for the shortfall, which I appreciate. However, that’s not really the point. Most customers don’t weigh their groceries every time they receive an order, so discrepancies like this can easily go unnoticed.

My suggestion to everyone is to check the weight of chicken, fish, or any other items sold by weight whenever possible. Hopefully, this was just an isolated packing error, but it’s worth being aware of.

title: I’m Russian. I came to India. And I need to say something about Blinkit.
text:
In Russia we have Yandex Lavka, Samokat, all these delivery apps. And compared to India — they’ve completely lost their minds. Free delivery only in the morning, only with some weird conditions, surge pricing every five minutes, “high demand”, “weather conditions”, “courier unavailable”, blah blah blah.

Meanwhile Blinkit in India:
free delivery half the time,
cheap as hell,
and FAST.

Me and my bro ordered a ridiculous amount of food and random stuff for like 1500 rubles total. Enough for a WEEK. In Russia that money gets you depression and maybe two energy drinks.

And the speed? Indian couriers DO NOT SLEEP. I swear this country runs on shift rotations like a sci-fi factory. One guy sleeps at 6 PM and wakes up at 3 AM, another sleeps at 2 AM and wakes up at 10. Delivery never stops. Day, night, apocalypse — doesn’t matter.

And somehow there’s STILL no night surcharge.
Meanwhile Yandex be like:
“high demand 🤓”

So if you’re in India giving Blinkit less than 5 stars — you are spoiled beyond belief. Go live in Russia for a month and then come back. You’ll start kissing the courier when he arrives in 8 minutes.

Blinkit 10/10 app.
